units: <cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 27:12">Targ. Ex. XXVII, 12</cite>; a. fr.—[Targ. II Esth. V, 1; VI, 5 <cite ref="D01029"><he>דרא</he></cite>; I Esth. <cite ref="D01135"><he>דרתא</he></cite>.]—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:1:22">Y. Snh. X, 28ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>עד דַּרְתֵּיה דר׳ וכ׳</he> (ed. Krot. <cite ref="D01134"><he>דַּרְתָּה</he></cite>) to the court of R. Ḥ.’s residence.

<cite ref="Yoma 72b:12">Yoma 72ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 31b:1">Sabb. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>דלית ליה ד׳ וכ׳</he> he who has no court, but makes a gate-way for his court (who possesses erudition but no fear of the Lord).—Pl. (<he>דַּרְתַּיָּא</he>) <he>דָּרָתָא</he>, <he>דָּרָאתָא</he>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Kings 21:5">Targ. II Kings XXI, 5</cite> (ed. Lag. <he>דָּרָת</he> constr.).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 10:8">Targ. Ps. X, 8</cite> <he>דורתיא</he> ed. Lag. (Var. <he>דדרתיא</he>, Ms. <he>דּוּרָאתָיָיא</he>).
<cite ref="Targum of I Chronicles 23:28">Targ. I Chr. XXIII, 28</cite> <he>דרתיא</he> ed. Lag. (ed. Rahmer <he>דראתא</he>).
B. Bath. 67ᵃ if he said דִּירָתָא, all agree, it meant houses; they differ only when he said דַּרְתָּא (Ms. O. דָּרָאתָא), the one says, the court is meant &c.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 67a:5">Ib.</cite> if he said <he>דָּרָאתָא</he> (Ms. M. <cite ref="D01135"><he>דרתא</he></cite>).
